purpose: Detect material changes in legislation, statutory instruments, commencement, case law, official procedures, source availability or official routes and map their potential impact to affected property rules, answers and snapshots.
mapping_rules: A legal change affects only the propositions and scopes actually connected to the changed authority unless further dependency is established.
An amendment date is not automatically the effective date.
Commencement and transitional provisions determine when a change applies.
A later case may affect interpretation without changing statutory text.
A procedural webpage change does not automatically change substantive law.
A source-access change may require re-retrieval without changing the underlying legal proposition.
Historical snapshots remain anchored to the law and evidence applicable to their target date.
Current answers may require reverification when the current legal or procedural source changes.
hard_stops: Never mark an answer obsolete merely because a related source changed.
Never treat amendment publication as commencement without checking the governing source.
Never rewrite historical answers using current law.
Never propagate a case-law change beyond the proposition and scope it actually affects.
Never silently update a published answer when the impact analysis is unresolved.
